exact_statement: Version 4 preserves version-3 conclusions at their original scope. New interface: for all Boolean signs G(s,X),H(s,Y) on a shared k>=1 uniform physical data block with disjoint private cubes X,Y, and point selector A_r on r>=1 physical bits absent from both children, p=2^-r, F=A_r G+(1-A_r)H, d=Pr(G!=H), the complete control-first physical stopping-tree signed entropy payment Pi=H(F)-pH(G)-(1-p)H(H) is at most [4+(4k+6log2(e)+4log2(e)/e)/r]Q, Q=2rp d. For r>=k it is at most14Q, including k=r=1 using the independently reconstructed literal-overlap endpoint. I(F)=Q+pI(G)+(1-p)I(H), with every shared data influence counted through actual branch weights. Calibrating all shared-only atoms of supplied normalized core references yields one explicit normalized point-selector reference with D_root=pD_Gcal+(1-p)D_Hcal and CE_root=pCE_Gcal+(1-p)CE_Hcal+Pi. Certified terminal allowances give complete path-plus-terminal rate max(14,L_G,L_H), independent of recursive block depth when each block satisfies r>=k. For even k>=4, actual quadratic bent G and its one-point-flip H satisfy Pi/Q>=(1-2^-r)[4+2(k-4)/r], so selector-only payment diverges along k/r->infinity, while no unbounded full FEI ratio is asserted. The width condition is not hereditary under active-control restrictions. Arbitrary interleaving, clipped-positive charges, universal terminal admission and payment of excess collision from a nonreused terminal reserve remain open.
